Bed steadiness and crossfades. Music stem 3 s level from 4 to 319 s spans only -34.55 to -31.49 dBFS (median -33.10); 1 s level median -33.15, 1st percentile -36.0. Under speech vs in pauses the 250 ms median is identical (-33.00 vs -33.02 dBFS); a least-squares fit puts the music in the mix at 0.94-0.995x (about -0.3 dB) in every 10 s block, so no ducking or pumping. Across all five 2 s equal-power crossfades the 1 s level stays within -30.8 to -36.1 dBFS: 65.15 s min -36.1 (+1.5 s), 74.10 s min -35.0, 171.95 s min -35.0, 217.85 s min -35.9, 226.80 s min -35.1. These dips are within the track's own variation. No drop-outs, no sample discontinuities (largest music sample step 0.164 at 321.12 s, inside the end hits).

Possible groove stumble, low confidence. Onset-envelope beat analysis (period about 1.14 s) puts the beat phase after the splice about 0.23 s off the phase before it at 65.15 s and 217.85 s (same splice used twice), and about 0.26 s off at 171.95 s; control points with no splice measure 0.00-0.07 s. With a 2 s overlap that can read as a brief doubled or flammed pulse rather than a level change. Phase coherence is weak (R 0.03-0.23), so confirm by ear; this does not affect level steadiness.

Over the end card this reads as a deliberate button, not a fault, but it clearly breaks the 'steady low bed'. Confirm it is intended. The bed then fades from about -30 to -57 dBFS in the last 0.2 s (324.03-324.23 s), a quick tail.
